record.paper_title: Mapping current and activity fluctuations in exclusion processes: consequences and open questions
record.context_brief: Comparison with KPZ scaling in spin dynamics
record.original_question: What is the precise relationship, if any, between the KPZ scaling governing activity fluctuations in the time-reversal-symmetric SSEP and the KPZ scalings recently found for SO(3) classical spin dynamics and for the quantum Heisenberg magnet?

evidence.quote:
The occurrence of such KPZ scaling could be interestingly compared
to those recently uncovered by Prosen and coworkers for SO(3) classical spin dynamics [115] or for the
quantum Heisenberg magnet [116].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the symmetric simple exclusion process (SSEP) on a one-dimensional lattice (e.g., a ring of L sites) with hard-core particles each attempting jumps to nearest-neighbor sites at rate 1, with the move accepted only if the target site is empty. The dynamics is reversible with respect to the uniform Bernoulli measure. The dynamical activity over a time interval [0,T] is defined as the total number of particle jumps performed by the system, K_T. Studying the large deviations of K_T/T together with finite-size (in L) corrections reveals, on one side of a dynamical phase transition for the activity, scaling exponents and a limit shape characteristic of the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) universality class.

Independently, KPZ-type scaling (with dynamical exponent z=3/2 and KPZ scaling functions) has been identified in the equilibrium spin-spin autocorrelations of:
(a) the classical isotropic Heisenberg (SO(3) symmetric) lattice spin dynamics, and
(b) the one-dimensional isotropic quantum Heisenberg magnet at high temperature.

Problem. Determine whether there is a precise mathematical relationship between the KPZ scaling that governs the activity large deviations of the time-reversal-symmetric SSEP and the KPZ scaling observed in the spin transport of the classical SO(3) Heisenberg spin dynamics and the quantum isotropic Heisenberg magnet. Specifically, identify a common underlying structure (such as an exact mapping, shared limiting nonlinear stochastic equation, or shared random matrix / Bethe-ansatz mechanism) that explains the appearance of KPZ universality in all three settings, or alternatively prove that the KPZ behaviors arise from genuinely distinct mechanisms.
artifact.category_tag: KPZ universality in exclusion and spin systems
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature confirms KPZ scaling in both SSEP activity large deviations and isotropic (classical and quantum) Heisenberg spin chains, including experimental verification on quantum simulators and theoretical work showing only "partial" emergence of full KPZ universality in spin chains. However, no work establishes a direct mathematical correspondence between the KPZ regime of SSEP activity fluctuations and the KPZ scaling in SO(3) classical or quantum Heisenberg dynamics, so the question of a precise relationship remains open.

status_evidence.title: Partial yet definite emergence of the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang class in isotropic spin chains
status_evidence.snippet: Superdiffusion exhibiting Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling ... isotropic Heisenberg spin chain shows superdiffusive transport
status_evidence.claim: KPZ scaling in isotropic Heisenberg chains is confirmed only partially; mechanism still under investigation.
